newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Tottenham players expected to comprise the squad for Sunday's F.A. Cup third-round match against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday:

Ian Walker, goalkeeper, age 25. Son of Norwich City manager Mike Walker, has established himself as understudy to England goalkeeper David Seaman. Has missed just one league match in last two-and-a-half years.
Sol Campbell, defender, 22. Recently made England debut. A strong versatile player who has been one of the few Spurs players to perform consistently well this season.
Colin Calderwood, defender, 31. Spent most of his career in the lower divisions with Mansfield and Swindon. Has been at Spurs for three years and played in all three of Scotland's matches in Euro 96.

John Scales, defender, 30. Recently joined Spurs for 2.6 million pounds ($4.4 million) from Liverpool and could be the player to bring some stability to the side. Missed the 7-1 mauling at Newcastle with a hamstring injury.
Stephen Carr, defender, 20. An Irish Under-21 international who made his Spurs debut aged 17 three years ago but then did not get another game until this season. Has established himself this season.

Clive Wilson, defender/midfielder, 35. The veteran left-back has been one of Tottenham's most reliable and consistent players since joining Spurs from QPR in June 1995. Has also played for Manchester City and Chelsea.

Darren Anderton, midfielder, 24. Has earned the nickname "Sicknote" because one thing or another always seems to be wrong with him and has hardly played for a season and a half. England international with superb skills who would add considerably to Tottenham's strength if and when he started playing regularly again.

Ruel Fox, midfielder, 28. Tricky winger who has twice moved for 2.0 million pounds ($3.4 million), from Norwich to Newcastle and from Newcastle to Spurs. Scores the occasional goal, has good vision and pace and does well in taking on and beating defenders.
David Howells, midfielder, 29. Been at Spurs for 12 years and played more than 300 matches. A defensive midfielder who often poses an attacking threat at set-pieces because of his prowess in the air.

Andy Sinton, midfielder, 30. Won 12 England caps in the early 1990s. Moved to Spurs from Sheffield Wednesday for 1.5 million pounds ($2.6 million) last January and recently scored his first goal for the club.
Allan Nielsen, midfielder, 25. Joined Spurs from Brondby in the summer after playing for Denmark in Euro 96 when he scored for his country against Turkey. Has scored in Spurs' last three matches.
Teddy Sheringham, forward, 30. Joined Spurs in August 1992 after playing for Millwall and Nottingham Forest. Outstanding in England's Euro 96 campaign, has looked jaded in recent weeks.

Steffen Iversen, forward, 20. It took manager Gerry Francis 18 months before he secured the Norwegian striker's signature last month. Tall, strong and powerful, he has assumed the No.18 shirt left vacant by the great Juergen Klinsmann.
Rory Allen, forward, 19. Made his debut this season. Has deputised for Chris Armstrong this season and looks to have what it takes to succeed at the highest level.

Ronny Rosenthal, forward, 33. Despite his years still fast and tricky but his lightning bursts down the wing often fail to produce much danger. Now spends most of his time on the bench and could well move on before the end of the season.

Chris Armstrong, forward, 25. Bought as replacement for Juergen Klinsmann for a club record fee of 4.5 million pounds ($7.7 million) in the summer of 1995. Scored 22 goals last season, currently sidelined with a groin injury.
Jason Dozzell, midfielder, 29. Made 400 appearances for Ipswich before joining Spurs in August 1993. No longer an automatic first choice.
